one_line: A shared measurable 3D room-planning canvas for humans and agents.
what_it_does: Lets a person and an agent inspect, compare, measure, edit, validate, and undo changes in the same 3D room state.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes semantic room objects, measurements, constraints, revisions, and undo rather than requiring coordinate-based UI driving; the shared live state is central to the product.
leverage_evidence: About text describes 21 native tools for inspection, comparison, measurement, layout application, spatial analysis, history, and targeted undo.
Writes use named objects, real measurements, relationships, expected revisions, collision and clearance validation, and visible human/agent attribution.
Video frames show iterative changes to the same rendered 3D room and accompanying activity/state panels.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent, unusually complete workflow from inspection and comparison through application, measured wall art, exact movement, analysis, history, and undo; frame sheets visibly show iterative room states and results.
execution_evidence: Three product-motion sheets show the same furnished room changing across successive states.
Description specifies a serializable domain engine, spatial validation, revision history, and rendered-revision synchronization.
Visible product includes a 3D room, object/state panels, and activity or result information.
impact_rationale: Room planning is a real iterative task for homeowners and designers, and precise constraint-aware collaboration addresses a concrete limitation of screenshot-driven agents.
impact_evidence: Pitch centers on moving and refining named furniture in a measurable room.
Product visibly supports clearances, circulation, fixed openings, and collision checks.
Shared human-agent refinement is directly demonstrated in the video frames.
creativity_rationale: A shared, measurable 3D spatial canvas with revision-aware human-agent collaboration is a fresh and deeply pursued interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Concept combines semantic spatial tools, procedural room rendering, constraint analysis, and targeted undo.
The demo pursues a concrete design story rather than a generic chat overlay.
Video shows multiple room arrangements and refinement stages.
usability_note: Rich validation and reversible changes support confident use, though the spatial interface is inherently complex.
red_flags: Exact tool-call text is not legible in the contact sheets.
standouts: Semantic spatial state and targeted undo make WebMCP materially consequential.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage with strong product-motion evidence and a distinctive, coherent workflow.

one_line: A consent-driven packing cockpit where human priorities and agent constraints meet.
what_it_does: Lets humans pin essential items while an agent proposes compliant repacking and only seals the bag after blocking violations are cleared.
leverage_rationale: Typed packing state, pinned-item invariants, threshold evaluation, consent gates, and irreversible sealing are much safer and more reliable through semantic tools than UI clicking.
leverage_evidence: Description says propose_repack cannot drop pinned items and seal_bag requires zero blocking violations.
Human accepts or rejects the proposal; the agent does not touch the bag without consent.
Video shows the packing dashboard changing gauge/status state across frames.
execution_rationale: The core cockpit and state progression are coherent, with a clear safety contract and multiple presets, but the frame sheets do not visibly prove the complete call-and-consent sequence.
execution_evidence: Two product-motion sheets show a consistent packing dashboard and changing status/gauge states.
Description specifies one bag, one scale, one manifest log, proposal, consent, and irreversible seal stages.
Three concrete failure-mode presets are described.
impact_rationale: Packing for air travel, family emergencies, or go-bags is a concrete need, and preserving must-carry items while satisfying thresholds offers credible value.
impact_evidence: Use cases include airline cabin rules, TSA constraints, family packing, and wildfire go-bags.
The demo visibly centers on item lists and threshold/status feedback.
The product addresses an asymmetric human-and-agent planning problem.
creativity_rationale: The constitutional distinction between human-pinned necessities and agent-enforced constraints is a memorable collaboration model.
creativity_evidence: Pinned items cannot be dropped by the proposal tool.
Consent before mutation and irreversible sealing are built into the concept.
Video presents a focused packing cockpit rather than a generic assistant.
usability_note: Dashboard, gauges, manifest, and explicit consent appear understandable; exact interaction details are only partially visible.
red_flags: No explicit tool-call transcript is visible in the frame sheets.
standouts: Strong human-safety contract around pinned items and sealing.
advance_reason: Clear high-value shared-state workflow with strong concept and credible visible product evidence.

one_line: A progression-gated Terraria companion that only knows what the player has unlocked.
what_it_does: Provides context-aware crafting, housing, and progression help while registering later-stage tools only as the player advances.
leverage_rationale: Stage-gated tool registration makes the agent's available knowledge and capabilities reflect live player progression, preventing spoilers and unsupported answers more reliably than a general agent.
leverage_evidence: Description says later stages are not registered as tools and three tools flip with the player's stage.
Demo scenarios provide game state without requiring the real game.
Frame sheets show Terraria context and a resulting Fog guidance interface.
execution_rationale: The product concept and visible guide flow are coherent, but the demo uses fake scenarios and a stand-in screenshot, limiting end-to-end evidence of live game integration.
execution_evidence: Video frames show Terraria-related context, a Fog interface, and generated guidance/result screens.
Description explicitly acknowledges fake scenarios and a stand-in screenshot.

impact_rationale: Players of progression games have a real spoiler-avoidance and recipe-discovery need, and scoped help can improve play without revealing future content.
impact_evidence: Pitch directly targets spoiler-prone Terraria assistance.
The assistant is designed around what the player has beaten and carries.
Visible frames show game-help results rather than only a landing page.
creativity_rationale: Progression-gated agent knowledge is a fresh interaction constraint that turns the game's fog of war into an assistant capability boundary.
creativity_evidence: Tool availability changes with player stage.
Concept explicitly addresses wiki spoilers and hallucinated recipes.

usability_note: A second-screen companion with demo scenarios is approachable, though live-game setup is not demonstrated.
red_flags: Demo relies on fake scenarios and a stand-in screenshot rather than a live game.

standouts: Capability/knowledge gating aligned to game progression.
advance_reason: Distinctive WebMCP gating idea and credible product/results evidence despite simulated game context.

red_flags: Tool calls are not explicitly readable in the frame sheets.
standouts: Strong shared spatial-state model and exportable evidence workflow.

standouts: Excellent bounded-capability and human-approval design for a health-adjacent app.

leverage_rationale: The product is itself an agent runtime and makes structured WebMCP discovery, persistent skills, versioned reuse, and repair the core capability; this is not a UI convenience layer.
leverage_evidence: Description defines a Native WebMCP → Cached Web Skill → Browser/DOM learning ladder.
Runtime stores versioned skills, validates outcomes, and repairs only failed dependencies.

execution_rationale: The described 11-action Learn–Reuse–Repair flow and visible runtime dashboard are coherent, but the contact sheets do not make every end-to-end transition legible.
execution_evidence: Description specifies a live taskboard demo surviving a Create Task → Add Task UI change with v1→v2 repair.
Frames show a consistent dark runtime interface with workflow/configuration sections.
Implementation stack and IndexedDB/extension architecture are specified.
impact_rationale: Repeated browser work is a widespread source of brittleness and wasted tokens; persistent validated skills offer credible value to agents and operators.
impact_evidence: Problem statement identifies repeated exploration, fragile clicks, and repair cost.
Runtime includes inspectable logs, timings, validation, and skill versions.
Product demo visibly focuses on workflow reuse rather than a one-off task.
creativity_rationale: Combining native WebMCP routing with semantic workflow learning, capability snapshots, dependency fingerprints, and targeted self-repair is an ambitious and memorable runtime concept.
creativity_evidence: Native-first fallback ladder is a strong interaction/system design.
Safe snapshots persist metadata rather than executable handlers.
Demo framing explicitly centers Learn once, Reuse, Self-repair.
usability_note: Inspector, execution log, timings, and validation make a technically complex runtime inspectable, though configuration is dense.
red_flags: Frame sheets do not clearly show readable tool invocation or a full repair result.
API-key/service dependency is described but not demonstrated in detail.
standouts: Most direct and ambitious WebMCP infrastructure concept in the packet.
advance_reason: Transformative agent-infrastructure concept with strong architecture and coherent visible runtime evidence.
